options.text: The deer gets the Sun's energy indirectly by eating the shoots that used sunlight to make food.
When the deer eats the shoots, energy passes from the deer to the shoots.
The deer eating shoots in the shade gets no energy linked to the Sun.
The deer can get the Sun's energy for growth just by standing in sunlight without eating.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Anaya watches a deer eat tender shoots under a shady canopy. She asks how the deer is linked to the Sun's energy through plant food.

part_answers.answer: Shoots store energy from sunlight as food; the deer receives that energy by eating the shoots, even in the shade.

teacher.key_rationale: Animals receive the Sun's energy indirectly through plants and food. Energy does not flow from deer to shoots; shade does not cut the link; standing in sun without eating does not supply food energy.
